claim: Across 44 quarterly readings of bank new-car loan rates from August 2015 to May 2026, the 72-month rate averaged only 0.1 point above the 60-month rate (median 0.115); it was at least half a point higher in just 1 reading and actually lower in 14. In May 2026 it was lower: 6.97% versus 7.14%. On $35,000 that means $596.21 a month instead of $695.36, and $1,206 more interest in total ($7,927 vs $6,721). Stretching the term at the same rate alone adds $1,412; at the average premium the rate itself adds only $118 of a $1,530 total. History, not a forecast.

assumptions: Loan amount $35,000, level monthly payments, no fees, no prepayment, no trade-in or negative equity rolled in.
Bank survey rates stand for what a typical borrower is offered; dealer/captive financing and credit-score tiers are not modeled.
Latest paired observation (May 2026) used for the dollar example; the average premium example adds the 2015-2026 mean premium to the latest 60-month rate.
